variants.role: photorealistic draft before user arcade direction
variants.prompt:
Use case: sketch-to-render.
Asset type: production 16:9 photorealistic Sengoku-era tactical game battlefield background, 2048x1152 or larger.
Input image 1 is the mandatory geometry/camera blueprint to render. Input image 2 is visual material quality/style reference only; do not copy its map layout or unrelated landmarks.
Primary request: Turn the crude geometry in image 1 into a detailed realistic period battlefield, with natural depth, tactile soil, irregular vegetation, hand-built earthworks, weathered wood, believable rock faces and coherent physically based light. Retain every playable road centreline, branch, gate entrance, crossing, water boundary and land clearing from the blueprint at the SAME normalized screen positions. Replace primitive models with convincing architecture/landscape rather than tracing their rectangular textures. Keep the exact orthographic oblique 50-degree camera, frame/crop and 16:9 canvas. No horizon/sky. Close battle area, not a miniature overview of the whole castle/region.
Scene: 1560, 마루네 요새 전투. 완만한 약 35m 구릉의 작은 흙담 요새와 마른 해자, 자연 숲. 근세 대천수·도시·눈·폭우를 넣지 않습니다. 요새는 북동, 남서·북서의 두 육지 접근로를 비웁니다.
Historical art constraints: 완만한 약 35m 구릉의 작은 흙담 요새와 마른 해자, 자연 숲. 근세 대천수·도시·눈·폭우를 넣지 않습니다. 요새는 북동, 남서·북서의 두 육지 접근로를 비웁니다.
Ground season: neutral; time of day: neutral_daylight; weather: unknown. Unknown weather means neutral restrained conditions, never invent snow, storm or catastrophe.
Road centreline coordinates measured from image top-left (x,y from 0 to 1): [{"id":"north","points":[[0.04,0.73],[0.15,0.56],[0.29,0.62],[0.43,0.49],[0.49,0.29],[0.64,0.26],[0.76,0.28]]},{"id":"ridge","points":[[0.04,0.73],[0.15,0.56],[0.45,0.21],[0.55,0.14],[0.67,0.18],[0.76,0.28]]}]. These lines must remain traversable and visually continuous, with no props growing across them.
Gate entrances at [[0.76,0.28]]. Place the actual gate opening on these points, not the roof peak. Nearby 16th-century garrison wooden buildings and earth banks, no restored modern multi-tier castle.
Open playable emplacement centres (do not cover with trees, roofs or water): [[0.7456,0.1813],[0.6669,0.3186],[0.5879,0.4285],[0.45,0.15],[0.366,0.3727],[0.3563,0.1628],[0.4596,0.5921],[0.2059,0.3387],[0.12,0.72],[0.87,0.36],[0.33,0.75],[0.3,0.54],[0.57,0.21],[0.45,0.27]]. Integrate these as naturally flattened land berms/roadside earth platforms, without circles, symbols or colored tiles.
Composition/materials: avoid broad empty flat lawn. The inter-road land has subtle relief, layered grasses, exposed earth, small roots, irregular believable foliage, modest rugged rises, worn approaches. Rich but readable game lighting, clear middle values on roads and depth at forest edges. Buildings, vegetation and terrain must share one realistic scale; roads fit small infantry formations, a gate door is roughly twice a human height. Trees border the play area rather than blanket it. Fine balanced texture, no over-sharpening, no depth-of-field blur.
Constraints: empty environment only, no soldiers, horses, people, arrows, bodies, UI, health bars, place labels, text, watermark, glowing signs, fantasy buildings, giant statues, cherry-petal effects, photo frame or miniature-diorama tilt shift. No rectangular water patches or repeated billboard trees. Preserve blueprint gameplay topology aggressively. Output one seamless full-frame battlefield image, not a collage or concept sheet.
Important: remove all four sample soldiers shown in the geometry input; retain only empty terrain. Use the second input's realistic natural forest/soil quality, never its gate placements. Give the fort a visible ground-level opening EXACTLY at x=0.76,y=0.28 within the final image. Camera and road geometry are fixed; no top-down drone aerial photo.

Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: production game terrain, wide 16:9 landscape.
Input image 1 is the current terrain render to edit. Input image 2 is a geometry blueprint that locks the camera and road coordinates.
Primary request: Restyle image 1 into a polished semi-realistic arcade RTS battlefield. The user likes rich texture/depth but finds documentary photorealism gritty and old-fashioned. Make it feel like a modern strategy game: confident readable terrain shapes, moderately stylized rocks and trees, grouped clean foliage, pleasantly fresh restrained colors, simplified microtexture, crisp playable ground, tactile painted/PBR surfaces and soft grounded shadows. Subtle art direction and physical materials rather than a photograph. More inviting and readable, less intricate forest noise. Do NOT go childish, toy-like, cuboid, flat lawn or mobile cartoon.
Keep invariants: exact 16:9 frame, orthographic oblique 50-degree view, exact two branching paths, north-east fort opening at normalized (0.76,0.28), all gate/fort positions, dry moat and low hill contours. Preserve the close tactical battle scale. No aerial-drone top-down view. No horizon/sky.
Scene: Marune low hill and small Japanese earthen/wooden fort, 1560. Humble Sengoku architecture and palisade, not a modern multi-tier white castle. Neutral daylight, no snow, no rainstorm. Distinct earth rise and worn dirt approaches.
Ground: slightly broader clean dirt roads, readable flattened emplacement clearings beside roads. Trees border the battlefield, reduce visual clutter in the inter-road clearings. Use deep forest edges and warm ochre soil with moderate lively natural greens; roofs/fort timber charcoal brown. No gritty all-brown gloom, no artificial neon, no cel outlines.
Playability: road centre lines remain in EXACT image positions from the geometry input. Roads start at (0.04,0.73), branch at (0.15,0.56), paths go through [(0.29,0.62),(0.43,0.49),(0.49,0.29),(0.64,0.26)] and [(0.45,0.21),(0.55,0.14),(0.67,0.18)] and both end at fort (0.76,0.28). The point (0.76,0.28) is the visible ground-level gate opening itself, not a roof.
Empty environment only. No soldiers, horses, people, text, labels, glowing markers, circles, interface, health bars, logos, watermark. One full-frame coherent game terrain image, not a grid or comparison sheet. Render at least 1672x941 or a higher-resolution 16:9 canvas.
